title: 55 per hour annual salary: what it means with casual loading and super
description: Convert $55 per hour annual salary for a 38-hour week. See how casual loading and super affect your pay, plus tax estimates and comparisons to award rates.
salarySummary: At $55 per hour for a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is $108,680 before tax, with super of $13,041.60 paid on top.

faqs.q: Does the $55 per hour rate include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The $55 per hour rate is your base rate. If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top, making your casual rate $68.75 per hour. That loading is part of your minimum entitlement under the Fair Work Ombudsman's award system. When you use the timesheet, you can tick a checkbox to add the 25% loading; never type a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is super calculated on a $55 per hour annual salary?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. For a full-time employee on $55 per hour working 38 hours a week, annual ordinary earnings are $108,680. Super at 12% is $13,041.60, but only up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Since $108,680 is below that cap, the full 12% applies. Your employer pays this into your super fund, separate from your take-home pay.

faqs.q: What is the take-home pay after tax for $55 per hour annual salary?
faqs.a: Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and a single Medicare levy of 2%, the estimated annual tax on $108,680 is about $25,567. That leaves an estimated take-home pay of $83,113 per year, or about $1,598 per week. This estimate assumes no HELP debt, no Medicare levy surcharge, and no salary sacrifice. Use the take-home pay page for a more personalised estimate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the $55 per hour annual salary

If you earn $55 per hour and work a standard full-time week of 38 hours, your annual gross salary is straightforward to calculate. Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours per week, then by 52 weeks:

**$55 × 38 × 52 = $108,680 per year**

This is the figure most people refer to when they talk about a **55 per hour annual salary**. It assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage at $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026, so $55 per hour is well above that minimum.

### The fortnightly view

Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. At $55 per hour for 38 hours a week, your weekly gross is $2,090, so your fortnightly gross is $4,180. This can be useful for budgeting if you are paid fortnightly, as many Australian employers do.

## Casual loading and super: what gets paid on top

A key point about the **55 per hour annual salary** is whether you are a permanent employee or a casual. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of their base hourly rate, as set out in most modern awards by the Fair Work Ombudsman. That means a casual on a $55 base rate would actually receive $68.75 per hour. The loading is meant to compensate for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

When you use [the timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate and can check a box to add the 25% casual loading. Never type a rate that already includes the loading – the tool handles it for you.

Superannuation guarantee is also paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super rate is 12%. For a permanent employee on $55 per hour, the employer pays an additional $13,041.60 into your super fund each year, assuming your earnings are below the $270,830 maximum contribution base. For a casual, the super is calculated on the base rate (or on the loaded rate? Actually, super is paid on ordinary time earnings, which for casuals includes the loading. Check: Fair Work Ombudsman says super is payable on the loaded rate if the loading is part of ordinary earnings. Yes, the 25% loading is ordinary earnings, so super is on the casual rate. So for a casual at $68.75 per hour, annual ordinary earnings would be $68.75 × 38 × 52 = $135,850. Super at 12% would be $16,302, still under the cap. But the article should clarify: super is paid on top of the loaded rate. However, the typical advice is that super is on ordinary time earnings, which for casuals includes the loading. So we'll state that.

### Comparing to award rates and averages

The $55 per hour rate is significantly higher than the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour. It is also above the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings reported by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) for May 2026, which was $2,083.70 per week – equivalent to about $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. So $55 per hour is just above that average. Note that the ABS average is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. For a job-specific figure, you would need to consult [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

If you are covered by an award, your minimum rate might be lower than $55, but many enterprise agreements or individual contracts pay above the award. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more detail on base rates.

## Tax on a $55 per hour annual salary

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the full tax-free threshold, the tax on $108,680 is estimated as follows:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on the next $26,800 ($4,020)
- 30% on the next $63,680 ($19,104)
- Total tax: $23,124
- Plus Medicare levy of 2% on all taxable income: $2,173.60
- Total tax and Medicare: $25,297.60 (rounded to $25,298)

This leaves an estimated take-home pay of about $83,382 per year, or $1,603 per week. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help you refine this with your personal circumstances, such as HELP debt or the Medicare levy surcharge.

### Super and salary packaging

Remember that super is paid on top of your gross salary, so your total remuneration package is $108,680 (salary) plus $13,041.60 (super) = $121,721.60. If you have access to salary packaging, such as for a car or novated lease, your taxable income may be reduced. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

## How to use this information

Whether you are negotiating a pay rise, comparing a job offer, or planning your budget, converting your hourly rate to an annual figure helps you see the bigger picture. The formula is simple: hourly rate × hours per week × 52. Always check whether the rate includes casual loading or not. For a permanent employee, the $55 per hour annual salary is $108,680. For a casual, the loaded rate of $68.75 per hour gives an annual gross of $135,850, with super on top.

You can also use [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) to go the other way – from annual salary to hourly rate. And if you are comparing job offers, remember that casual employees get loading but no paid leave, so the total value may differ.

## Important notes and disclaimers

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, refer to the [about the timesheet](/about) page or the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide.
